purpose: Same-scene RTX 4090 render comparison with the local Appendix300 candidate disabled and enabled.

render.camera: Newton endoscope camera, 1280x720; calibrated pinhole; 1 spp, 0 bounces
render.mapping: Cylindrical UV projection on appendix FEM rest nodes; bilinear GPU sampling; UVs follow FEM nodes

variant_a.candidate: Appendix300 v21 48 px overlapping patch candidate

variant_b.candidate: Appendix300 v22 exploratory 80 px overlapping patch candidate

texture_variant_render_comparison.visual_review: The 80 px variant is nearly indistinguishable from v21 at this camera scale; no evidence supports promoting either candidate.

interpretation: The GPU render uses the candidate texture on the appendix FEM boundary, and the texture-on render visibly changes the appendix appearance. This confirms the transfer/render path only. The candidate remains a prompt-mask-derived temporal RGB texture, not a camera-to-mesh registered surface reconstruction or calibrated albedo.
failed_or_pending_gates: Appendix identity in the source ROI is not expert verified.
No video-to-3D surface registration or validated UV correspondence exists.
The current target FEM surface is coarse and visibly faceted.
The rendered frame remains visually broad and does not pass blinded laparoscopic appearance review.
Lighting/specular separation and observed RGB to albedo calibration are absent.
No held-out real-video visual evaluation has been run.
privacy: Source video, texture pixels, and render images remain local in git-ignored output folders; this report contains aggregate metrics and public-source provenance hashes only.
